info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 0.5 hour final exam + 104.5 hours self-study
info.description:
This course develops English–Vietnamese and Vietnamese–English interpreting competence through authentic tasks situated in academic, public-sector, and workplace contexts. Learners analyze sources of meaning loss and apply equivalence strategies; manage register and shades of meaning to produce concise, accurate formal outputs; evaluate argumentative discourse and make justified ethical decisions; and interpret policy, political, and domain-specific discourse with verified terminology. Culture-bound references, implicature, humor, Latinisms, and loan expressions are treated with appropriate transfer strategies. Teamwork, turn-taking, co-interpreter support, and professional conduct are embedded throughout. AI is used as a probe with human verification and ethical safeguards. All activities and assessments align with the course CLOs and contribute to relevant PLOs.
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
- Apply advanced interpreting principles to produce context-appropriate renditions across academic, public, and workplace settings.
- Analyze and select target-language expressions to control register and shades of meaning.
- Evaluate argumentative discourse and uphold professional ethics while collaborating effectively in co-interpreting roles.
- Integrate domain knowledge (policy, socio-economics) into interpreting decisions to ensure accuracy and appropriateness.
info.studentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by the teacher after class
- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes
- Read the textbook in advance

clos.loDetails: Analyze sources of meaning loss and apply equivalence strategies to preserve propositional and pragmatic meaning.
Demonstrate teamwork (turn-taking, co-interpreter support) and professional conduct (punctuality, confidentiality).
Apply advanced interpreting principles across academic, public, and workplace settings to deliver context-appropriate renditions.
Evaluate argumentative discourse and justify ethical decisions in interpreting, including AI ethics (privacy, bias, attribution, confidentiality).
Analyze register levels and shades of meaning and determine appropriate target-language choices, using AI suggestions as probes with human verification.
Produce formal-register interpretations that are concise, accurate, and stylistically balanced.
Analyze policy speeches and render coherent interpretations of key claims and supporting evidence.
Apply core political/economic concepts to ensure domain accuracy in interpreting, and verify terminology with trusted resources and AI quality-checks.
Analyze culturally bound references, implicatures, and humor and choose appropriate transfer strategies.
Apply accurate equivalents or illustrate effective paraphrases for Latinisms and loan expressions, noting usage constraints.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to interpreting in a business setting.
assessments.note: Teacher is asked to write a field trip proposal with specific details and send it to the person in charge; or organize a project that facilitates the subject.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 1-3) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈100words/text), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 4-6) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈100words/text), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test the student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 7-9) to simultaneous interpreting.
assessments.note: The teacher shall prepare 5-6 audio files (≈2minutes/file) relating to several specific topics, of which the students will be informed in advance. On the test day, students will be divided into groups of 4 or 5. All members will be standing at different positions in class, simultaneously listening to the same audio and recording their interpretation using a smartphone. Upon completion, students are asked to send the record to the teacher immediately.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to consecutive interpreting (both ENG-VIE and VIE-ENG processes). Topics: 1. Education 2. Entertainment 3. Technology 4. Environment/Nature 5. Business, Economics and Finance 6. Tourism 7. Family and Friends 8. Health 9. Culture 10. Arts
assessments.note:
The length of one audio is 220-250 words.
Students take the exam individually. Students will randomly pick 2 topics to interpret. Students will listen to one audio in English for E-V interpretation, and listen to audio or the examiners reading a text in Vietnamese for the V-E process.
Students are allowed to take notes in the exam room.
